- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 10–15% below peak.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or negative; add 2–5% to initial forecast values.
- If history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day average.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast curve using 7-day moving average if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- When sentiment is zero for 5+ consecutive days, model often underperforms; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for lack of market signal.
